title: Telestream Integrates MPEG-H Audio to Streamline Media Delivery Ahead of Brazil’s DTV+ Roll Out
body_html:
Telestream has integrated MPEG-H audio into its media delivery solutions, a move that is particularly significant ahead of Brazil's DTV+ rollout. This integration is expected to streamline media delivery by providing a more efficient and flexible audio encoding solution. By supporting MPEG-H, Telestream is enabling broadcasters and media companies to deliver high-quality audio that is also adaptable to various playback environments, from mobile devices to home theaters.

What Was Announced

Telestream's integration of MPEG-H audio is a strategic move to support the upcoming DTV+ rollout in Brazil, which is expected to bring advanced audio features to the country's digital television landscape. The integration will allow Telestream's customers to take advantage of MPEG-H's capabilities, including object-based audio and immersive sound. This development is the result of Telestream's efforts to enhance its media delivery solutions and provide better support for next-generation audio formats. The company's decision to integrate MPEG-H audio reflects its commitment to staying at the forefront of audio technology and providing its customers with the tools they need to deliver high-quality content.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The integration of MPEG-H audio into Telestream's media delivery solutions has significant engineering and operational implications. By supporting MPEG-H, Telestream is enabling its customers to simplify their audio workflows and reduce the complexity associated with delivering multiple audio formats. This integration also allows for more efficient use of bandwidth, as MPEG-H can deliver high-quality audio at lower bitrates than traditional audio codecs. Furthermore, the use of MPEG-H enables the creation of immersive audio experiences, which can enhance the overall quality of the viewing experience. From an operational perspective, the integration of MPEG-H audio will require broadcasters and media companies to re-evaluate their existing workflows and consider how they can take advantage of the new capabilities offered by this audio format.

Industry Context

The integration of MPEG-H audio into Telestream's media delivery solutions reflects the broader trend towards the adoption of next-generation audio formats in the broadcast and media industries. As consumers increasingly expect high-quality audio experiences, broadcasters and media companies are under pressure to deliver content that meets these expectations. The use of MPEG-H audio is part of a larger shift towards more immersive and interactive audio experiences, which is being driven by the adoption of new technologies such as object-based audio and audio over IP. Other companies, such as Fraunhofer IIS, are also working on the development of MPEG-H audio, and the format is expected to play a key role in the delivery of next-generation audio services. The integration of MPEG-H audio into Telestream's solutions also highlights the importance of interoperability and compatibility in the broadcast and media industries, as companies seek to ensure that their solutions can work seamlessly with a wide range of devices and platforms.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

The integration of MPEG-H audio into Telestream's media delivery solutions has significant implications for broadcast and media teams, who will need to consider how to take advantage of the new capabilities offered by this audio format. Engineers and operations managers will need to evaluate their existing workflows and consider how they can be adapted to support the delivery of MPEG-H audio. This may involve investing in new equipment and training staff on the use of new technologies. Additionally, broadcast and media teams will need to consider the potential impact of MPEG-H audio on their existing infrastructure, including their playout, ingest, and distribution systems. As the industry continues to evolve, it is likely that we will see further adoption of MPEG-H audio and other next-generation audio formats, and broadcast and media teams will need to be prepared to adapt to these changes in order to remain competitive. By understanding the implications of MPEG-H audio and other new technologies, broadcast and media teams can position themselves for success in a rapidly changing industry. The key to success will be to balance the need for innovation and experimentation with the need for reliability and consistency, and to ensure that new technologies are deployed in a way that supports the overall goals of the organization.
